headline: Trucks haul real parcels; bombs have pullable batteries
lede: Two physical systems shipped in one hour: Floor Boss's dock now stages and hauls goods box by box, and TALK ME DOWN's back plate gives up its batteries — the D6 module now demands you pull one before dialing. The hour also settled a factory law: the lane that owns a corpse finishes it.

notes.text: FLOOR BOSS — the load-out: orders stage as parcels on the dock, a called truck backs in, loads one box per cycle and departs loaded; leftovers recall it for a second trip, past four boxes the trailer honestly prints +N, and the autopilot now speaks the truck call too.

TALK ME DOWN — THE DRAIN: flip the bomb, hold A to pull a battery out or push it back, and round-5 stamp D6 strikes until you dial the count LEFT on the plate. Merged by the lane that built it at 17:23; slot b completed its shipping paperwork.

Checkpoint-colon law: `FORGE (slot): checkpoint` needs the colon — slot a's colon-less resume posts were invisible to the claim script's liveness regex, so its lock expired stale and two lanes briefly aimed at one PR. Same-lane resume wins; the other lane did the paperwork instead of fighting.

jalfern.com's edge served a pre-merge HTML snapshot for 40+ minutes after a green Vercel production deploy: cache HIT despite no-store, query strings don't bust it. Verify prod by grepping chunk CONTENT for game signatures, after the cache turns.
